recipes.name: Apple Crumble Pie
ingredients_raw: 5 cups apples - peeled, cored and thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C.)
Arrange apple slices in unbaked pie shell. Mix 1/2 cup sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over apples.
To make the crumble topping: Place 1/3 cup sugar and flour in a bowl. Cut in cold butter with 2 knives or pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs; spoon mixture over apples.
Bake in preheated oven until apples are soft and top is lightly browned, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Crumble Pie
raw_recipe.description: This apple crumble pie has a classic apple pie filling with cinnamon and is topped with a rich and buttery crumb topping for a cozy fall dessert.

review.reviewBody: OH MY GOD is this pie DELICIOUS!!! I followed the suggestions of others, and did the following: (1) added about 1/4 cup of flour to the apple mixture to absorb apple juices; (2) instead of mixing apples with 1/2 cup white sugar, I used 1/4 white sugar and 1/4 brown sugar; (3) in a bowl, mix the apples and sugars and cinnamin before putting it in the pie (as opposed to sprinkling the sugar on top of the apples in the pie crust); (4) I used the basic flaky pie crust also on this website which was great; (5) i sprinkled some flavored walnuts on top of the pie with the crumb mixture; and (6) I cooked it at a lower temperature for an hour and 15 minutes. This pie was so delicious that i cannot wait to make it again. Everyone raved about it. ENJOY!

This is the best apple pie I have ever made!! I started making it in September and by Thanksgiving I had family demanding it. This is not a pie that you'll have leftovers of (some people were even complaining because they didn't get a slice). These are a few things I have changed: I coat my apple slices in flour first. It makes the filling more jelly then runny (you will notice the flour will make a doughy type flim on the apples before you put them in the pie crust). Then I put a layer of apples, then coat them in sugar, then put another layer and coat, then one more layer (my apples are usually heaping by now) and last layer. I am VERY generous with my sugar. It makes it a bit sweeter but not too sweet. I don't change much, just I found if I don't coat my apple slices, the filling is really runny when it's finished, and if I don't put the extra sugar, the pie is a bit more tart. Enjoy the best apple pie around!!

Hmm.. easy and flavor was good but…. Made for fantastic apple crumble soup. We used 1/2 white and brown sugar, added more cinnamon but like others, forgot to coat apples in flour. Certainly will add this to our family recipe book.

I took advice from other posters, I added 1/4 cup flour to the pie filling and mixed the sugar, cinnamon and flour with the apples in a gallon ziploc before dumping into the crust. I added about a teaspoon of almond extract to the pie filling. I also used a store-bought rolled crust.

For the crumble, I used half flour and half almond flour plus I mixed in a 1/4 cup of flax meal. I used 1/4 cup of sugar in the crumble, and you could definitely go a little lighter, especially if you plan to serve with ice cream or make a salted caramel drizzle for the top.

I cooked at 375 for 1 hour and 15 minutes... so yummy!!!

I made this pie three times. I love it. I used Granny Smith (sour) and Fuji(sweet). It's actually missing the step (as someone suggested) to dredge the apple slices with flour. One version, I forgot to do this and there was a bit of fluid from the apples; still got eaten. I could have drank the fluid, so delish! My most successful bake, I used 1/4 cup flour and coated the apples. I used brown sugar vs white for the interior of the pie and I took the suggestion to layer. I used three layers of apple slices and put the spices on top of each layer. Yummm. For the crumbs, I had a little melted butter and sprinkled it over the pie. This let the crumbs brown more evenly. To allow for quicker baking, I sliced the apples a little bit below 1/4". each. Time-consuming. The recommended 40 minutes bake time is not enough if you're not doing a deep dish. I didn't have a deep dish pan. So I did 45 on two pies and 53 on one pie. Without a glass pan, I couldn't see if the crusts browned. The 53 minutes burned the covered outer crust but produced the crispiest pie. So I'd even go 50 minutes to ensure the light browning you want of the crumbs and to give you a lovely crispy crust. Definitely recommend this recipe!

I LOVED this recipe! It was so easy! ? followed another poster’s advice on small changes: 1) adding 1/4 flour to the apples to absorb juices 2) on the apple mixture, do half white sugar and half brown sugar, 3) I also crushed ginger snap cookies I had in the pantry and sprinkled those on top of the apples but beneath the crumble, 4) I cooked at 375 for approximately 45-50 minutes. I also used a refrigerated pie crust because I don’t have skills for pastry yet! Good luck and try not to eat the whole pie on your own!!

I agree. This has to be my favorite apple pie, with the exception of my Mom’s, as no mortal can draw near her appleness… I’ve tried the recipe as is and it is wonderful. I too have fallen to the lure of using both white and brown sugar, 1/4 cup each, and I mix the apples with the sugar and an additional 1/4 cup of flower before putting them into the pie crust. I make the crumble as specified but I do add some chopped pecans on top of the apples before adding the crumble topping. If you do this make sure the pecans are under the crumble. They can burn at pie cooking temps. Enjoy!

We love this recipe too! I did add a little extra cinnamon, dash of nutmeg and half brown/half white sugar with a tablespoon of flour and tossed the apples first before placing in the dish. I cooked for about 55 minutes at 350 and 5 minutes at 400 to brown the topping. YUM!!

Awesome, easy, basic recipe. I used all brown sugar instead of white. Added 3 tablespoons of flour, a bit of nutmeg, and fresh squeezed lime juice to the apple mixture. I coated the apples in a separate bowl before putting them into the pie crust with. I also used Brown sugar in the crumble topping instead of white. Turned out fabulous!

Amazing apple pie! As other reviewers suggested, I mix 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 brown sugar, 1/4 cup flour, and a heaping teaspoon of cinnamon to the apples in a bowl before dumping it all in the pie crust. Once cooled, the pie filling was thick and perfect! The amount of crumble topping was perfect. Yum!

I used this recipe as the base for my pie. I took the advice of others here and it came out awesome. I used my spiralizer to ribbon cut 10 medium apples that were peeled. If you place your core in the right spot it also cores your apples. I mixed apples with 1/4 C each brown and white sugar (the filling was a bit tart- next time I’ll add more), 1tsp cinnamon and 1/4 C flour. I piled it into the pie crust and double the topping by adding more butter and a box of vanilla pudding. 
Baked on 400 for 25 minutes and 350 for 35 minutes.
good!
Made exactly as instructed. I loved it. My daughter said she liked it but wasn’t a fan of the crunchy topping.
Made as written . The toping is so good and makes the pie moist.
The crumble wasn't that great
I used brown sugar in the apples to give it more flavor but still white sugar in the crumble.
The pie was too sweet for my tastes. If I make it again I would cut the apples into bigger chunks and use less sugar.
One of the best pies I've had

Nothing fancy about this pie which is why I liked it so much, an apple forward pie. Comfort food at it's best. Like others I did toss the apple slices with the sugar and cinnamon. The second time I made it I realized I forgot to add the cinnamon when I was ready to pop it in the oven. I sprinkled a little cinnamon sugar over the crumb topping and my husband said he likes it better that way!

This recipe is sooooo easy and what a pleasant aroma throughout our home. I made it 3x . Came out perfect every time. Delicious! I always go to this website for easy and good recipes! Thank you for sharing! My hint.. I added more apples and sprinkled a little of the sugar and cinnamon on the bottom of the pie crust. Peace and blessings to all
